meta.title: Diego Olalla · Java Back-end
meta.description: Portfolio of Diego Olalla, a Software Engineering student at FIAP focused on Java and Spring Boot back-end.

hero.name: Diego Olalla
hero.lead: Software Engineering student at FIAP, learning back-end with Java and Spring Boot.

about.photoAlt: Diego wearing glasses and a black T-shirt, resting his head on his hand
about.p1: I study Software Engineering and the back-end is the part I like most, the side behind the screen: APIs, business rules and data.
about.p2: I currently work as a freelancer building landing pages, and soon I'll move on to more complex systems. At the same time, I'm building a solid base in Java and studying Spring Boot and SQL. I learn best by building projects, and their code is here.

projects.intro: Study and freelance projects, with what makes each one interesting.

p1.title: Sito's Estacionamento
p1.desc: A marketing landing page I built as a freelancer for a parking business with two locations in Méier, Rio de Janeiro. It shows each location's prices, maps with a 360° tour and an "Open now" status calculated in São Paulo's time zone.
p1.learned: Local SEO with JSON-LD, isolated JS modules with import(), a lite mode that turns off heavy effects on slow machines, and cache busting with versioned URLs.

p2.title: JavaNelio
p2.desc: Exercises from Nelio Alves' Java course. The InterestService interface calculates interest and has two implementations, BrazilInterestService and UsaInterestService.
p2.learned: Interfaces, polymorphism and default methods. Each country follows the same contract with its own rate.

p3.title: This portfolio
p3.desc: Built with plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no framework. It comes in Portuguese and English, has a light and a dark theme, and an animated topographic map at the top that reacts to the mouse.
p3.learned: IntersectionObserver, fetching JSON, custom events, Canvas and accessibility.

wip.title: Next project: a Spring Boot API
wip.desc: I'm studying to build my first REST API with Spring Boot and a database. Follow along on GitHub.

journey.intro: How I got here, in order.

i1.title: The start
i1.desc: I took one semester of Computer Science and fell in love with logic and with building projects in languages like Java and Python.

i2.title: Software Engineering
i2.desc: I now study Software Engineering at FIAP, focusing on back-end development.

i3.title: Data Structures and Algorithms
i3.desc: I'm taking data structures and algorithms courses to get a more solid base and write more efficient code.

i4.title: Freelance landing pages
i4.desc: I build landing pages for clients as a freelancer, and soon I'll move on to more complex systems.

next.title: Back-end internship or junior role
